babycare.sleeptraining_method_gentle_pickup_desc: Soothe your baby, then calmly put them back down.
babycare.sleeptraining_method_chair_desc: Sit beside the crib and move a little further away every few nights.
babycare.sleeptraining_method_fading_desc: Slowly reduce rocking or feeding to sleep over several days.
babycare.sleeptraining_method_timed_checks_desc: Short, calm check-ins at gradually longer intervals.
babycare.sleeptraining_gp_step_1: Put your baby down drowsy but awake.
babycare.sleeptraining_gp_step_2: If crying continues, pick them up and soothe until calm.
babycare.sleeptraining_gp_step_3: Put them down again once calm and repeat as needed.
babycare.sleeptraining_gp_step_4: Keep the same steps at every nap and every night.
babycare.sleeptraining_chair_step_1: Sit beside the crib and stay quiet and calm.
babycare.sleeptraining_chair_step_2: Move the chair a little further away every few nights.
babycare.sleeptraining_chair_step_3: Leave the room once your baby settles without you close by.
babycare.sleeptraining_fade_step_1: Use the same routine every night.
babycare.sleeptraining_fade_step_2: Slowly reduce one sleep support, such as rocking or feeding to sleep.
babycare.sleeptraining_fade_step_3: Change only one thing at a time over several days.
babycare.sleeptraining_fade_step_4: Offer comfort without taking your baby out of the crib.
babycare.sleeptraining_fade_step_5: Celebrate small progress and keep going.
babycare.sleeptraining_tc_step_1: Choose check-in times, for example 5, 10 and 15 minutes.
babycare.sleeptraining_tc_step_2: Check in briefly with a calm voice and pick up only if needed.
babycare.sleeptraining_tc_step_3: Lengthen the interval gradually as your baby settles.
babycare.sleeptraining_plan_intro: Pick one gentle method and stick with it for 14 days. Mark how each day went.
babycare.sleeptraining_plan_young: Night wake-ups are normal under 4 months. Sleep training usually starts around 4 to 6 months. Talk to your pediatrician first.
babycare.sleeptraining_plan_finished: The 14 days are over. Review the results with your pediatrician.
babycare.sleeptraining_steps_subtitle: Tick the steps as you try them
babycare.sleeptraining_calendar_subtitle: Tap a day to mark how it went
babycare.sleeptraining_plan_stop_note: Stop and seek medical advice if your baby is unwell, not feeding well or has breathing concerns.
babycare.sleeptraining_safe_back: Always place your baby on their back to sleep.
babycare.sleeptraining_safe_firm: Firm, flat mattress with only a fitted sheet.
babycare.sleeptraining_safe_empty: No pillows, bumpers, blankets or toys in the crib.
babycare.sleeptraining_safe_share: Share the room but not the bed, especially with a young baby.
babycare.sleeptraining_safe_sofa: Never let your baby sleep on a sofa or armchair.
babycare.sleeptraining_safe_temp: Keep the room comfortably cool and avoid overheating.
babycare.sleeptraining_safe_smoke: Keep your home and car smoke-free.
babycare.sleeptraining_warn_breath: Pauses in breathing, struggling to breathe or grunting breaths.
babycare.sleeptraining_warn_blue: Blue or grey lips or skin.
babycare.sleeptraining_warn_limp: Very hard to wake, limp or unusually floppy.
babycare.sleeptraining_warn_feeds: Refuses feeds, with few wet diapers or a dry mouth.
babycare.sleeptraining_warn_fever: Fever of 38 °C or higher in a baby under 3 months, or fever with unusual sleepiness.
babycare.sleeptraining_safety_subtitle: Go through it in your baby’s sleep space
babycare.sleeptraining_safety_done: Great. Your baby’s sleep space follows the safe sleep basics.
babycare.sleeptraining_safety_hint: Tap each point you have checked
babycare.sleeptraining_disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. If you are worried about your baby’s sleep, breathing, feeding or growth, talk to your pediatrician.
babycare.sleeptraining_live_subtitle: Tap when your baby falls asleep and when they wake up
babycare.sleeptraining_live_hint: Sleeps shorter than 5 minutes are not saved
babycare.sleeptraining_tip_nap: Dark, quiet room. Put your baby down drowsy but awake and use the same cues for every nap.
babycare.sleeptraining_tip_bedtime: Start the bedtime routine 20 to 30 minutes beforehand. An earlier bedtime often helps an overtired baby.
babycare.sleeptraining_tip_morning: Open the curtains and start the day with daylight and a feed.
babycare.sleeptraining_tip_awake: Watch for tired signs such as yawning, rubbing eyes or fussing, and start winding down early.
babycare.sleeptraining_timeline_subtitle: Typical rhythm for your baby’s age. Tap a block for a tip.
babycare.sleeptraining_wake_hint: The plan is built around it
babycare.sleeptraining_schedule_note: Approximate times. Follow your baby’s tired signs and shift the plan earlier or later.
babycare.sleeptraining_step_crib_drowsy: Into the crib, drowsy but awake
babycare.sleeptraining_routine_subtitle: The same steps in the same order every evening
babycare.sleeptraining_routine_done: Tonight’s routine is complete. Sweet dreams!
babycare.sleeptraining_routine_hint: Tap each step when it’s done
babycare.sleeptraining_manual_subtitle: Forgot to tap? Add it by time
babycare.sleeptraining_manual_hint: For a night that ended this morning, choose Yesterday.
babycare.sleeptraining_chart_subtitle: Total sleep per day. Tap a day for details.
babycare.sleeptraining_avg_empty: Shown after you log a few days
babycare.sleeptraining_ranges_subtitle: Typical ranges for this age. Every baby is different.
babycare.sleeptraining_insight_no_data: No sleep recorded yet. Use the sleep tracker on the Today tab to see patterns.
babycare.sleeptraining_insight_need_more: Log at least 3 full days for a reliable review.
babycare.sleeptraining_insight_naps_below: Fewer naps than typical for this age. Try a nap in the middle of each awake window. If not every nap is logged, this can be normal.
babycare.sleeptraining_insight_nap_short: Naps are shorter than typical. Check that the room is dark and quiet and that your baby is not overtired.
babycare.sleeptraining_insight_night_short: The longest night stretch is shorter than typical. Night feeds may be the reason. Talk to your pediatrician if it continues.
babycare.sleeptraining_insight_wake_long: Awake windows look long. Shorter windows often help babies this age sleep better.
babycare.sleeptraining_insight_wake_short: Awake windows look short. Give your baby a little more awake time before naps.
babycare.sleeptraining_insight_total_below: Total sleep is below the typical range. If you log every sleep, an earlier bedtime can help.
babycare.sleeptraining_insight_all_good: Your logs are within the typical ranges. Keep it up.
babycare.sleeptraining_hero_idle_detail: Pick a wake-up time to see the plan
babycare.sleeptraining_save_failed: The sleep could not be saved. Please try again.
babycare.sleeptraining_too_short: Under 5 minutes, so it was not saved
babycare.sleeptraining_too_long: This sleep looks too long. Discard it and add the real times with Add a past sleep.
babycare.sleeptraining_manual_future: The end time is in the future. For last night, choose Yesterday.
babycare.sleeptraining_manual_length: A sleep must be between 5 minutes and 16 hours
babycare.sleeptraining_delete_failed: The sleep could not be deleted
babycare.sleeptraining_no_birthdate: Add your baby’s birth date in the profile to see age-based guidance.
babycare.sleeptraining_out_of_range: This guide is for babies aged 1–12 months.
